corazon.title: Corazón Napoletano
corazon.headline: A new opening built as one connected system.
corazon.support: Identity, content, menu, physical experience, website and acquisition designed together from day one.
corazon.scope: Identity · Content · Menu + Upselling · QR · Website · Acquisition

hero.support: A new opening where identity, content, menu, in-venue experience, website and acquisition were designed as one connected system.

context.heading: A new opening means making many decisions before having real data.
context.body: Corazón Napoletano started from zero. The opportunity was to build brand, experience and digital presence at the same time, preventing each touchpoint from growing as an isolated piece.
context.body2: The challenge wasn't simply being online. It was making sure what someone saw in an ad, found on the website, read on the menu and experienced in the restaurant told the same story.

system.title: We didn't design pieces. We designed how they connect.
system.support: Each element had a different function, but all of them had to reinforce the same perception and make the next action easier.

identity.heading: Before communicating the brand, we had to build it.
identity.body: We defined an identity able to live both on screen and inside the restaurant, seeking coherence between what the brand promises and what the customer finds.

content.heading: Show the real product, not a generic version of the restaurant.
content.body: Content direction was built around product, preparation, atmosphere and people. Content designed to make the brand recognisable and to feed both organic channels and acquisition.

menu.heading: The menu is part of the strategy too.
menu.body: We reorganised information, hierarchies and choice paths to make the offer easier to understand and create upselling opportunities without turning the experience into commercial pressure.
menu.principle: Helping people choose better can help the business sell better.

qr.heading: Digital can start at the table too.
qr.body: We integrated QR access into the physical experience to reduce the steps between discovering the offer and choosing, keeping visual continuity with the rest of the brand.

website.heading: The website continues what starts outside it.
website.body: We designed and built an experience able to present the brand, show the menu and shorten the distance between interest and booking, with navigation adapted to different languages.

acquisition.heading: Building the system was only half the job. People still had to reach it.
acquisition.body: We activated acquisition campaigns on Meta Ads and Google Ads, connecting creative, message, search intent and digital experience to generate demand around the new opening.
acquisition.closing: Campaign and destination are optimised better when designed as parts of the same journey.

result.label: Revenue increase
result.body: From the month following the launch of the new system, Corazón Napoletano recorded a 20% increase in revenue.
result.statement: We don't attribute the result to one individual piece. Brand, content, menu, experience, website and acquisition were designed to reinforce one another.
result.note: Result specific to this project and context.

barber.title: Barber Booking
barber.headline: Rethinking booking from both sides of the chair.
barber.support: A booking platform designed for barbershops, exploring how to simplify the customer experience while giving the business more control over scheduling, services, professionals and data.

hero.support: Barber Booking explores a booking experience built for barbershops: simple for the person making the appointment and useful for the business managing it.

problem.heading: Two different experiences share the same calendar.
problem.body: The person booking wants to find a slot and finish in a few steps. The person managing needs to know who's coming, which service they chose, with which professional and how the business is doing.
problem.closing: The product has to simplify both sides.

customer.label: Booking
customer.body: Reduce unnecessary decisions and make finding an available slot immediate.

business.label: Managing
business.body: Give the business a clear operational view without forcing it to jump between different tools.

customer.heading: Fewer steps between intent and appointment.

alts.serviceSelection: Service selection in Barber Booking, mobile app
alts.availability: Availability calendar for booking an appointment in Barber Booking
alts.bookingSummary: Booking summary and confirmation in Barber Booking

business.heading: The booking ends for the customer. For the business, that's where operations begin.

list.title: Clear information
list.body: Availability, services and professionals without ambiguity.

list.title: Useful data
list.body: Statistics designed to help understand, not decorate a dashboard.

adaptability.body: Barber Booking starts from the needs of a barbershop. Many of its patterns — services, professionals, availability, customers and schedule — also exist in other appointment-based businesses. The priority, however, is to solve one context well before generalising it.

status.heading: In development.
status.body: The product keeps evolving as we validate flows, interface and architecture. We show it as part of NEXO Lab because the process also represents how we think about product and technology.
